Against c3d17ab08bd5db65dc5ffe69e41f7b2ff0c2fc49, the issue-501 pin, the commit adds records/n0175, n0232 and n0264 (.sqpk and .sqcert) and changes README.md; those seven files and the licence are retained. The retained files are byte-identical with the licence beside them. Issue #528 credits Daniil Ostashev with the three packings, names the pieces each composition uses and their sources, and states AI assistance: the author set up and drove an AI-assisted research loop, and AI agents wrote and ran the search, composition and verification code.
claims: Issue #528 reports s(175) <= 13.76417431748659662942782322004234282577, s(232) <= 15.76417431748659662944782322004234282577 and s(264) <= 16.77473513238783284261026458732177098083, certified and rounded up; each records/n0NNN.sqcert gives the exact side, dilated by 1 + 1e-60 from the 60-digit optimum of its contact topology, and the README at the pin prints the same sides rounded up to 15 places.

The issue says all three are new arrangements and not refinements: compositions of two library rectangles in opposite corners plus aligned squares, each using a new packing of 38 unit squares in an (h + 2) x h rectangle with h = 5.76417431748659662929..., found by a GPU soft-to-rigid search after Yohei Nakajima's idea; 175 with David Ellsworth's s(171) template, whose pieces are cut from Thomas Schadt's s(50), 232 with a 76-square piece of Erich Friedman's s(85), and 264 with a 93-square piece of Evan Daniel's exact optimum of Joost de Winter's s(126).

The issue restates issue 501's sides at the same commit, s(155) <= 12.95242540695845613565..., s(156) <= 12.97917261364442607531... and s(211) <= 14.99633672133631569465..., the c3d17ab certificates, which a8db6ff does not change.

The author reports that its own C++ checker (sqverify) accepts all three in GMP rational arithmetic and that a separate 80-digit mpmath cross-check accepts them; each side is reported as the exact first-order optimum of its contact topology with nonnegative KKT multipliers. These are author reports; no optimality is claimed.
